title: Murine Skin Abscess Model for Studying Bacterial Infection Dynamics
author: Gupta, Sircombe, et al.
materials: Pierce Rapid Gel Clot Endotoxin Assay Kit

steps.title: Acclimate and house mice
steps.instruction: House Swiss Webster (or CD‑1 / C57BL/6) mice for a minimum of three days before any manipulation; keep them under BSL‑2 conditions; no specific‑pathogen‑free housing required.

steps.title: Shave and depilate skin
steps.instruction: One day before infection, anesthetize the mouse (see step 3) and shave the intended injection site with properly positioned clippers to avoid abrasions; apply depilatory cream, leave for the recommended time, then thoroughly rinse to remove all residue and prevent burn marks; verify complete hair removal before proceeding.

steps.title: Anesthetize mice with isoflurane
steps.instruction: Induce anesthesia with 3–5 % isoflurane in oxygen for 30 s to 1 min; maintain with 1–2.5 % (up to 3 % if needed) during shaving, depilation and injection; after the procedure stop isoflurane and provide oxygen until normal movement resumes.

steps.title: Grow bacteria to mid‑log phase
steps.instruction: Inoculate the chosen strain (e.g., P. aeruginosa LESB58, PAO1, PA14, S. aureus USA300, etc.) from a frozen stock; grow overnight, then on Day 0 adjust the culture to an OD₆₀₀ of 0.1 in a conical flask. Perform a growth‑curve analysis for each strain to determine the time required to reach mid‑log (≈2 h for fast‑growing S. aureus, 4–6 h for slower P. aeruginosa). Grow at 37 °C in a shaking incubator until the culture reaches the mid‑log phase.

steps.title: Wash bacterial cells
steps.instruction: Harvest the culture by centrifugation at 5 364 g for 4 min at room temperature (18–22 °C); discard supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 1 mL sterile PBS; repeat the spin and wash once more under the same conditions; finally resuspend the pellet in 1 mL sterile PBS and ensure the suspension is homogeneous.

substeps.instruction: Remove supernatant, add 1 mL PBS, resuspend.

steps.title: Adjust inoculum to target CFU
steps.instruction: Measure the OD₆₀₀ of the washed suspension and adjust with sterile PBS to obtain the OD that corresponds to the desired colony‑forming units (CFU) per 50 µL injection according to the strain‑specific OD‑CFU correlation (Table 2). Use 50–100 µL for subcutaneous injection; injection volume is 50 µL per mouse.

substeps.instruction: Refer to Table 2 for each strain:
• P. aeruginosa LESB58 – OD ≈ 2.1 → 5 × 10⁹ CFU/mL (target 2 × 10⁷–1 × 10⁸ CFU/mouse).
• P. aeruginosa PAO1 – OD ≈ 0.55 → 2.5 × 10⁷ CFU/mL (target 1 × 10⁷–5 × 10⁷ CFU/mouse).
• P. aeruginosa PA14 – OD ≈ 0.11 → 5 × 10⁶ CFU/mL (target 2 × 10⁶–1 × 10⁷ CFU/mouse).
• S. aureus LAC USA300 – OD ≈ 2.5 → 5 × 10⁸ CFU/mL (target 1 × 10⁷–5 × 10⁷ CFU/mouse).
• A. baumannii Ab5075 – OD ≈ 2.0 → 1 × 10⁹ CFU/mL (target 5 × 10⁸–2 × 10⁹ CFU/mouse).
• K. pneumoniae KPLN649 – OD ≈ 2.0 → 1 × 10⁹ CFU/mL (target 5 × 10⁸–2 × 10⁹ CFU/mouse).
• E. coli E385 – OD ≈ 5.0 → 2.5 × 10⁹ CFU/mL (target 1 × 10⁹–5 × 10⁹ CFU/mouse).
• E. coli MG1655 – OD ≈ 5.0 → 1 × 10⁸ CFU/mL (target 2.5 × 10⁸–1 × 10⁹ CFU/mouse).
Adjust with PBS until the measured OD matches the required value.

steps.title: Check endotoxin and protein levels
steps.instruction: Aliquot 500 µL of the final bacterial suspension into endotoxin‑free reaction tubes and measure residual endotoxin using the Pierce™ Rapid Gel Clot Endotoxin Assay Kit (A43879); the assay detection limit is 0.03 EU mL⁻¹. In a separate tube, aliquot 100 µL and determine protein concentration with the Pierce BCA Protein Assay Kit (Thermo Scientific, 23225); protein must be ≤1 µg mL⁻¹. Both parameters must be below their thresholds before proceeding.

steps.title: Determine viable CFU count
steps.instruction: Set aside 20 µL of the final suspension, perform serial dilutions in a 96‑well plate, and plate on appropriate agar to enumerate CFU; this confirms the actual inoculum delivered. If downstream transcriptomic analysis is planned, keep an extra aliquot for DNA/RNA extraction.

steps.title: Prepare injection inoculum
steps.instruction: Resuspend the bacterial pellet in endotoxin‑free sterile PBS (or saline or glucose solution); do NOT use pure water because of osmotic imbalance and potential tissue necrosis. Use 50 µL (or 50–100 µL) per mouse for subcutaneous injection.

steps.title: Subcutaneous injection
steps.instruction: While maintaining anesthesia, inject the prepared 50 µL bacterial suspension subcutaneously into the previously shaved and depilated area of each mouse to initiate the skin abscess.

steps.title: Optional polymicrobial preparation
steps.instruction: For co‑infection studies, prepare each bacterial strain separately, adjust each to the desired OD, then combine the suspensions immediately before injection in the required volume ratio (e.g., 1:1). Verify that the combined inoculum remains within the tolerated CFU range for the mouse strain.

description: This protocol outlines a murine skin abscess model using a high-density bacterial inoculum to study infection progression and evaluate antimicrobial treatments. Immunocompetent mice typically develop a localized skin infection within a standardized 3-day experimental window (Figure S1) when established bacterial pathogens are used. Kaplan–Meier curves in Figure S1 show 100% survival across multiple bacterial strains and inoculum doses. New organisms should first be assessed for their ability to induce infection. Bacterial infections can be tracked non-invasively using bioluminescent or fluorescently labelled bacteria.1 This protocol uses clinical, multidrug-resistant strains Pseudomonas aeruginosa LESB58 and Staphylococcus aureus LAC USA300. However, the model is broadly compatible with other well-characterized pathogens1,2 and suitable for co-infections.3,4 Bacterial concentration should be optimized to establish robust infection while avoiding levels that compromise mouse welfare. Before testing therapeutic compounds, toxicity screening is required. We have assessed diverse compounds, including peptides,5 peptidomimetics,6 nanogels,7 liposomes,8 nanoparticles,9 and antibiotic combinations.10 Swiss Webster (SW) mice were used, though CD-1 or C57BL/6 are also suitable. Housing does not require specific pathogen-free conditions. A minimum three-day acclimatization is recommended. All infections and handling should occur in a Biosafety Level 2 (BSL-2) laboratory under appropriate containment conditions. Basic proficiency in handling laboratory mice is essential, although the required manipulations are relatively straightforward. Depending on the planned downstream processes, proficiency in data acquisition and interpretation is necessary.
